findings: The raw collective writes receiver storage without increasing the tensor version.
An ordinary no_grad copy_ and detached copy_ both increment the receiver version.

In PyTorch 2.9, a requires-grad leaf that is itself a view of a non-grad base can lose the old child view's edge to that intermediate leaf after any normal in-place copy. The no-collective plain-copy control reproduces this behavior.
Owned leaves and base leaves retain their local gradients under all normal copy variants.
The implementation preserves the source version and saved graph by avoiding copy-back on the source rank.
Final tests recreate receiver forward views after an update to a non-owning leaf, and also verify existing views of nn.Parameter leaves. This is not differentiation through the collective.
The data-copy diagnostic preserves the old version, but was rejected for production because it bypasses ordinary autograd mutation tracking.
